process_recording.layout: One process-lifetime file: magic followed by append-only complete JHLOG segments. Every segment has its own header, dictionaries, quality and SHA-256. FINAL chunk commits delimit segments; the last segment may be open or torn.
process_recording.identity: All segments carry the same RunID and ProcessInstanceID. SDK reconfiguration changes SessionID, not the physical file or application run. Snapshot rotation preserves the collector epoch and digest chain.
process_recording.snapshot: A captured process file is a bounded byte frontier. A sealed rotation at this frontier does not prove that a separate file is missing. Torn bytes remain explicit; coverage still requires collection-window evidence.
process_recording.compatibility: Raw JHLOG 5.x files remain readable. Readers that do not support the process marker reject it before reading any events. No manifest or per-epoch extraction is required.

build_identity_contract.states: unknown=0, unminified=1, mapped=2. Only mapped carries exactly 32 digest bytes; other states carry none.
build_identity_contract.reasons: unknown state only: unspecified=0, missing_asset=1, unreadable_asset=2, malformed_asset=3, unsupported_asset_schema=4, namespace_mismatch=5. Known states require reason=0.
build_identity_contract.identity: Digest of exact post-R8 mapping bytes, generated as an APK/AAB asset after R8. Libraries use the host identity. APK/AAB and instrumentation artifact hashes are recorded separately after packaging.
build_identity_contract.legacy: Schema2 remains readable as unverified. Older readers reject schema3 explicitly. Header schema is independent of unchanged data-record format5.1.0.
build_identity_contract.policy: Matching SHA permits mapping; mismatch rejects mapping. Legacy or unknown identity requires explicit trust override and unverified labeling. No mapping is needed for unminified identity.

causal_concurrency_contract.schema: See specs/009-concurrency-diagnostics/contracts/causal-event-v1.md. Direct semantic record; never a five-bit micro-page row. Presence bits 0..21 distinguish measured zero from unavailable data. RESOURCE phase7 USE_ENTERED begins observation of an existing resource passed to use; acquisition and open/closed state are unknown. COROUTINE phase6 STATE_MACHINE_OBSERVED records first observed execution state without claiming creation.
causal_concurrency_contract.compatibility: Readers of 5.2 also read 5.0 and 5.1. Earlier readers reject required bit32. Old records remain unchanged; absence of causal records in old logs is unknown coverage, not observed zero.

symbol_origin_contract.dictionary_kind: With bit31 dictionary kind is (baseKind << 2) | origin. Front coding remains scoped by baseKind. References retain their prior encoding; origin is resolved from the referenced dictionary definition.
symbol_origin_contract.legacy: Without bit31 all origins are unknown. Stable IDs do not imply source provenance. Old readers reject required bit31.
symbol_origin_contract.mapping: Apply mapping to runtime_class and official Retrace to runtime_stack only. Preserve source_label and unknown text.

http_first_byte_contract.measurement: HTTP_TTFB_OBSERVED marks first-byte semantics, not successful observation. With HTTP_TTFB_KNOWN, ttfb_ms is the interval from the first requestHeadersStart of the Call to the first positive plaintext transport read containing its response byte, before HTTP parsing. HTTP/2 uses the first byte of the HEADERS frame for the actual stream ID; partial frame headers preserve the first-fragment timestamp.
http_first_byte_contract.scope: Includes request upload and retries before the first response, excludes preceding DNS/connect/TLS. The first informational or redirect response counts. This is an application-observed read time, not a kernel arrival or remote server timestamp. Request and response intervals can overlap this interval and must not be summed as disjoint phases.
http_first_byte_contract.unknown: Known zero is a valid sample. Without HTTP_TTFB_KNOWN the observed-semantics value must be zero and is not a timing sample. Missing/unsupported hooks, unavailable clocks, refused registrations, cache-only responses and failure before a response leave timing unknown. This is timing coverage, separate from event delivery completeness.
http_first_byte_contract.legacy: Without HTTP_TTFB_OBSERVED, preserve the recorded legacy field but exclude it from actual first-byte statistics, mathematical analysis and comparisons. Historical EventListener header-read intent is not a first-byte observation. Readers without required feature 28 reject new logs.

gauge_sum_contract.payload: With required feature bit 27, every GAUGE appends sum_high:uvarint after mode. Existing sum is the unsigned low 64 bits. The exact sum is sum_high * 2^64 + sum; zero low word is not a missing-value sentinel when sum_high is nonzero. COUNTER layout is unchanged.
gauge_sum_contract.legacy: Without bit 27, GAUGE has no high word and decodes sum_high=0. Old readers reject bit 27. Historical saturated SDK sums cannot be reconstructed.
gauge_sum_contract.bounds: Unsigned 128-bit sum, positive count; average-mode sum is at most count * max. A sum below max is invalid only for additive modes; LAST and STATE retain their historical last-value semantics.

http_body_contract.totals: When HTTP_BODY_TOTALS is set, the existing request/response byte fields sum observed body bytes across all exchanges of one Call, including authentication retries and redirects. Headers and transport overhead are not included.
http_body_contract.known: Existing request/response bytes-known flags independently identify an exact whole-Call total. The totals marker alone does not imply completeness. Incomplete exchanges, invalid counts and saturation clear knownness for that direction while preserving observed lower bounds.
http_body_contract.legacy: Logs without the marker remain readable. With attempts > 1 or redirects > 0, historical SDK byte fields may contain only the last exchange; treat their whole-Call totals as incomplete even if historical known flags are set. Preserve recorded byte values as lower bounds.
http_body_contract.android_saturation: The SDK saturates accumulated body bytes at Long.MAX_VALUE and clears the corresponding known flag. Repeated body callbacks within one exchange must not add bytes twice.

worker_registration_contract.name: REGISTERED_OBSERVED
worker_registration_contract.meaning: An asynchronous WorkManager query returned WorkInfo with the exact submitted UUID after successful Operation completion. This proves observed registration, not insertion time or acceptance of this enqueue attempt.
worker_registration_contract.lifecycle: An observation may precede or follow STARTED/FINISHED and may describe an already existing, completed or periodic request. It does not create a future-start expectation or a queue-time sample. Null, failed and cancelled lookups emit no registration claim; no polling is performed.
worker_registration_contract.legacy: ENQUEUED=1 remains readable as legacy evidence with its historical matching semantics. MissingEnqueue counts starts without a legacy enqueue timestamp and does not prove data loss.

stall_contract.legacy_5_0_0: stack_ref and duration_ms only; decode incident_id=0 and state=unknown
stall_contract.identity: Opaque nonzero ID scoped to one runtime session, preserved across its segments. Zero means a standalone observation without lifecycle correlation.
stall_contract.duration: Watchdog 5.1.0 measures uptime milliseconds since the last main-thread heartbeat. Ongoing and interrupted durations are observed lower bounds; recovered ends at the first subsequent heartbeat.
stall_contract.states: unknown=0; ongoing=1; recovered=2; interrupted=3. Zero ID is valid only with unknown or recovered.
stall_contract.sequence: A nonzero ID has ongoing observations followed by at most one terminal state. A terminal-only observation is valid when earlier segments or records are missing. No update may follow a terminal state.
stall_contract.comparison: Unknown, ongoing and interrupted evidence must not pass a configured exact stall-duration regression check.

http_collection_state_contract.feature: Required bit30 makes SESSION collector bit11 the effective HTTP feature state (available AND enabled). An absent bit means disabled only when feature30 is present. Historical logs keep unknown HTTP collection state.
http_collection_state_contract.scope: This declares permission to collect instrumented HTTP completions, not universal application network coverage. Quiet counts also require continuous sealed input and absence of relevant loss; the flag alone cannot prove an observed zero.
http_collection_state_contract.collection_window: QUALITY entries 0x204b (collection_window_start_elapsed_ms) and 0x204c (collection_window_end_elapsed_ms) are immutable clock bounds, not loss counts. Start is rounded up after feature-gate activation; end is sampled before its first deactivation or writer admission closure. A missing, reversed or changing bound means unknown coverage. Values persist across rotation; only a complete terminal chain proves the interval. Startup and writer drain are excluded.

worker_progress_contract.schema: version=1, stage=1(request)|2(omission summary), instance_id:u64, run_attempt:u32, generation:u32, observed_elapsed_nanos:u64, omitted_updates:u32, omitted_keys:u32, truncated_fields:u32, metadata_count<=8, then key:string<=512 UTF-8 bytes, type:string<=32 UTF-8 bytes, known_size:0|1, optional payload_bytes:u64 for each field. Stage2 has no fields, omitted_keys or truncated_fields.
worker_progress_contract.semantics: Records only direct setProgressAsync calls through the optional JankHunterWorker/JankHunterCoroutineWorker base implementations; a call does not prove persistence. Actual persisted progress is observed separately through WorkInfo. At most32 request records per attempt and one per second; omitted calls have a bounded summary at finish. No Data values are retained. CLI attributes only to one unambiguous active attempt in the same process session and otherwise reports unattributed evidence. Old logs remain readable; old readers may reject record38.

work_registry_contract.packet_header: version=1, snapshot_id, query_started_elapsed_ms, observed_elapsed_ms, interval_ms, packet_index, packet_count, total_observed, retained_jobs, unavailable_reason, row_count: unsigned varints. Up to128 retained jobs,8 rows per packet,16 packets; unavailable reasons0=available,1=no_source,2=query_failed,3=query_timeout,4=invalid_source. Unavailable packets contain zero jobs and counts.
work_registry_contract.row: uuid:string36, instance_id:u64, state:uvarint(0=enqueued,1=running,2=succeeded,3=failed,4=blocked,5=cancelled), attempt:u32, generation:u32, initial_delay_ms:u64, presence:u64. bit0=period+flex unsigned durations, bit1=earliest_eligible_unix_ms signed zigzag, bit2=stop_reason signed zigzag. Other presence bits rejected. Then tags:string_list8, omitted_tags:u32, network_type:string64, constraints:u64, URI strings:list4, omitted_triggers:u32, progress and output metadata lists8, omitted_progress:u32, omitted_output:u32, truncated_fields:u32. Texts max512 UTF-8 bytes; UUID canonical lower-case. Metadata: key:string512,type:string32,known_size:0|1,optional payload_bytes:u64.
work_registry_contract.constraints: Unsigned mask: bit0 charging,bit1 battery-not-low,bit2 storage-not-low,bit3 device-idle,bit4 content-URI,bit5 custom-network-request. Reserved bits rejected. These are declarations, not observations of device conditions.
work_registry_contract.bounds: Each packet <=128KiB; one pending batch in writer. CLI12500 packets/100000 rows/conservative32MiB retained packet budget. Loss and partial snapshots remain explicit; packet assembly scoped by run/process/session plus snapshot_id, never UUID alone.
work_registry_contract.semantics: Supported WorkInfo observations only; class, unique name, dependency UUIDs, enqueue policies and backoff/expedited/quota are unknown in this source. Absence is not completion. RUNNING has unknown actual start. Periodic attempt counters can reset. Latest configuration generation need not be the generation currently executing. Earliest eligibility is not an appointment. CPU/resource attribution is not inferred.
work_registry_contract.compatibility: Old readers reject unknown record30. Existing layouts unchanged. Header anchors provide monotonic-to-calendar mapping; missing anchors and snapshot age remain unknown.

worker_catalog_contract.payload: UTF-8 JSON document preceded by unsigned varint byte length, max 131072 bytes. schema=1, status=available|missing|unreadable|oversized. Available documents carry original pre-R8 class names (max4096, unique, each max1024 UTF-8 bytes), namespace (32 hex), scope=application-and-packaged-dependencies-pre-r8, dynamic_modules=outside-base-scope, unresolved_classes and omitted_workers counters. Unavailable documents contain no inventory or coverage counts.
worker_catalog_contract.scope: Per collector epoch and process, loaded on maintenance. Pre-R8 candidates do not prove retention by R8 or runtime usage. Classes are never instantiated or kept alive by the inventory. Missing event is unknown, never an empty catalog.
worker_catalog_contract.bounds: Android reads at most 128 KiB plus one bounded read buffer; CLI retains at most32 documents and reports omitted documents. HTML displays at most100 class rows per page.
worker_catalog_contract.compatibility: Old readers reject unknown record29. Existing record layouts are unchanged.

worker_stop_contract.outcome: WORKER outcome5 is STOPPED, distinct from CANCELLED4. Stop caused by constraints, timeout or quota must not imply application cancellation. Unknown stop reason remains absent. Legacy readers reject unsupported outcome5; existing outcome values remain unchanged.
worker_stop_contract.concurrency: Unmatched starts contribute an observed point to concurrency, never an invented lifetime through the end of the log. Durations and resource correlation require a captured finish.

thread_snapshot_contract.type: 28; payload schema 1, 2 or 3; unsigned varints: schema, elapsedRealtime ms, scan duration ms, configured interval ms, clock ticks/sec (0 unknown), complete boolean, failed reads; bounded UTF-8 reason; row count <=2048.
thread_snapshot_contract.row: Unsigned TID, start ticks since boot; bounded UTF-8 name <=1024 bytes; unsigned OS state ASCII, user ticks, system ticks; zigzag signed 64-bit priority and nice. No flags or packed states. Unknown schema rejected explicitly. Counters are preserved, never wrapped or inferred from wall time.
thread_snapshot_contract.fidelity: Process/run/session from envelope header. Complete means successful enumeration/read, not atomicity or coverage between scans. Schema1 has no Java identity/state. Schema2 links only weakly registered live Java Threads on actual executing Linux TID, registered before scan start and still alive after state capture; native/uninstrumented threads remain unknown. First run hook is not creation/start and does not cover short-lived threads absent from snapshots. A full self-contained snapshot survives rotation or earlier losses; loss accounting uses existing event-reason counters.
thread_snapshot_contract.bounds: At most one pending snapshot per async writer, 2048 reads per scan, 4096 characters per stat read. File.list directory enumeration allocation depends on actual kernel task count. Default disabled pending complete overhead validation; explicit threadSamplerEnabled enables 5000ms interval, minimum500ms.
thread_snapshot_contract.java_schema_2: Schema2 appends unsigned presence(0|1) after EACH kernel row. Present: unsigned positive Java ID, daemon boolean, first observed elapsedRealtime nanoseconds; UTF-8 Java name <=1024 bytes, Java state name <=32 bytes, first run-hook source <=1024 bytes. States NEW/RUNNABLE/BLOCKED/WAITING/TIMED_WAITING/TERMINATED are separate from OS states. After ALL rows: unsigned dropped Java registrations. Schema1 unchanged; old readers reject schema2 explicitly. JSON emits Java ID and nanoseconds as decimal strings to preserve 64-bit precision.
thread_snapshot_contract.java_schema_3: Schema3 preserves schema2 and appends unsigned owned-by-Jank-Hunter flag (0|1) after each present Java source. The flag is true only for a thread explicitly registered while executing with its own Linux TID; missing Java identity or schema1/2 leaves ownership unknown. After all rows: unsigned dropped Java registrations. No name or package heuristic proves ownership.

uid_traffic_contract.feature: Required bit29 FEATURE_UID_TRAFFIC appends traffic_uid_plus_one and traffic_known_flags as unsigned varints after the ten existing DEVICE_CONTEXT values. Without the bit, historical payloads have no provenance.
uid_traffic_contract.uid: Zero means unknown. Android UID0 is encoded as1; maximum encoded UID is2^31. Flags use bit0 for RX-known and bit1 for TX-known; other bits and known-without-UID are invalid. A known counter may be zero. Unsupported counters have a clear known bit, independently per direction.
uid_traffic_contract.origin: SystemContextSampler records the process UID and TrafficStats support before sanitizing negative counters. Caller-supplied manual context has no invented UID. Changes in UID or known flags pass adaptive sampling.
uid_traffic_contract.scope: SDK RunID is a live process cohort protected by held OS file locks. The counter domain is RunID plus UID, never PID. Different runs never share a baseline. Continuous source samples across rotation require matching run/process/session/collector-clock identity, consecutive segment indices, a clean sealed rotation and matching previous digest.
uid_traffic_contract.aggregation: Union half-open byte-counter ranges to count each observed byte once. Unknown UID collapses counter ranges inside that run for a lower bound; unknown run identity collapses all runs. Reset, missing boundary, unsupported observations and overflow prevent exactness. Math assigns each byte to the first observation-end bucket confirming it, not inferred packet-arrival time.
uid_traffic_contract.compatibility: New CLI reads prior5.0/5.1 without provenance as uncertain. Old readers reject bit29. Numeric aggregate fields remain, with independent exact/lower_bound/unknown direction evidence. Only exact direction passes a requested traffic CI gate or contributes a traffic time series. Delivery completeness remains separate. Collection explanations appear only in mathematical analysis data-quality.

async_epoch_contract.epoch: One continuous collection session. Stop, disable and reconfigure close it; segment rotation preserves it. Existing run/process identity and event payload layouts are unchanged.
async_epoch_contract.tokens: Opaque primitive identity only; no retained writer, runtime session, UI object or timestamp truncation. Completed and previous-epoch tokens cannot write into a replacement epoch.
async_epoch_contract.boundary: Unfinished observations and completions already being published are recorded separately before final quality sealing. These counts describe a telemetry boundary, not proof that the application operation never finished or an invented lost-delivery count.
async_epoch_contract.rejections: Stale, duplicate, invalid and feature-disabled completions are separate observations. Counts while no epoch can record them are retained for the next epoch and do not count as its event delivery losses.
async_epoch_contract.capacity: HTTP, SQL call and Worker observation slots are bounded and never evict active work. Exact active transaction stacks remain proportional to depth without this slot limit. Invalid completion, capacity or identity exhaustion makes diagnostic completeness unknown (-1), because the missing event count cannot be inferred from the observation count. Completions still publishing at the final snapshot also make completeness unknown: that snapshot does not establish their delivery outcome. No lost-event count is invented.
async_epoch_contract.http: captureHttpContext registers a tracked HTTP operation. Generic same-epoch context remains supported for a single completion with an explicit legacy coverage count; unfinished HTTP observations cannot be enumerated through that legacy API. Unverifiable epoch identity is rejected.
async_epoch_contract.report: Jank Hunter CLI reports remain problem-first. All collection diagnostics are placed only in the dedicated data-quality section of the mathematical-analysis inspect/compare pages.

runtime_graph_storage_contract.quota: Each generation reserves at most 8 MiB for producer metadata, stack arrays and aggregate pages before allocating them, including old and new arrays during stack growth. The at-most-two-generation lifecycle bounds these quotas to 16 MiB; this is not a whole-SDK or process RSS limit. Shared string contents, consumer tables, writer queues and JVM-owned ThreadLocal maps are outside this storage quota.
runtime_graph_storage_contract.lifetime: Oversized empty stacks release arrays at full unwind. Drained terminated producers and stopped generations release storage independently of Thread object reachability. A bounded cache of 16 detached empty pages remains charged until reused or discarded.
runtime_graph_storage_contract.known_edge_loss: Denied semantic edges are included once in runtime_graph_input_total and runtime_graph_producer_capacity_loss. Accepted edges retain existing emitted/lost accounting.
runtime_graph_storage_contract.unknown_edges: runtime_graph_storage_skipped_entry_total counts omitted method entries. It does not determine an absent-edge count. Any positive count makes diagnostic_completeness_percent=-1 and level=unknown; requested completeness gates cannot pass. Stack context stays unknown across the omitted interval.
runtime_graph_storage_contract.compatibility: Existing event layouts and JHLOG 5.1.0 remain unchanged. Readers predating this quality counter explicitly reject it when present, rather than silently claiming completeness. New readers continue to read historical logs.

work_chain_edge_contract.schema: 1: unsigned varints version, parent UUID most/least raw 64-bit words, child UUID most/least raw 64-bit words, observed elapsedRealtime nanos, flags (bit0 caller source truncated; other bits rejected); required nonempty UTF-8 caller source (max512 bytes).
work_chain_edge_contract.meaning: An observed public WorkContinuation.then call declared a direct prerequisite between two request UUIDs in one collection epoch. It does not prove enqueue, acceptance, registration, or execution. Missing beginWith/then observations leave lineage unknown; combine and uninstrumented code are outside this source.
work_chain_edge_contract.bounds: Epoch-owned weak continuation identities, at most64 continuations and8 tail UUIDs per continuation by default. quality id0x2053 counts rejected/truncated declarations. Existing BULK admission records transport loss. Older readers reject record34 explicitly; older records remain unchanged.

work_chain_root_contract.schema: Same versioned payload as record33 WorkSubmission: UUID words, observed elapsedRealtime nanos, unique name/policy, caller source and truncation flags.
work_chain_root_contract.meaning: Public WorkManager.beginWith or beginUniqueWork returned WorkContinuation. The request UUIDs and optional unique name/policy describe graph construction, not enqueue, acceptance or execution. A later then event may declare dependencies. No direct acceptance is inferred from this record.
work_chain_root_contract.bounds: Only first8 request UUIDs per call. Extra requests and tracker rejections use quality id0x2053. Older readers reject record35; earlier records remain unchanged.

worker_failure_contract.schema: 1: unsigned varints version, salted instance ID, run attempt, generation, observed elapsedRealtime nanos, flags (bit0 stack truncated; other bits rejected); required exception class UTF-8 max128 bytes; optional frame-only stack UTF-8 max1024 bytes.
worker_failure_contract.meaning: An exception observed during a worker attempt, not its final WorkManager result. The record carries no exception message or field values. Match only to the same process/session instance ID, attempt, and generation.
worker_failure_contract.bounds: At most8 frames and1024 UTF-8 stack bytes at capture. Existing BULK admission records transport loss. Earlier readers reject record36; earlier records remain unchanged.

coroutine_segment_contract.schema: 1: unsigned varints version, monotonic process-local coroutine token, collection generation, entry Java Thread ID, exit Java Thread ID, segment start elapsedRealtime milliseconds, segment end elapsedRealtime milliseconds, state (0=suspended,1=completed,2=failed,3=cancelled); required source/owner UTF-8 max512 bytes. Version2 inserts positive entry and exit Linux TID varints before the source string. Version3 is a running-at-capture observation: state=4, end timestamp means observed-through time, entry Linux TID is positive, exit Java ID and exit Linux TID are zero/unknown.
coroutine_segment_contract.meaning: An observed synchronous resume segment of a Kotlin coroutine state machine, not ownership of the thread while suspended. Version3 does not terminate the segment; a later version2 exit record with the same token may follow. Token joins segments only within the same process/session and generation. Schema2 directly records both Linux TIDs; schema1 needs a separate observed Java-to-kernel mapping. Missing records or uninstrumented coroutines mean incomplete coverage.
coroutine_segment_contract.bounds: Only emitted with COROUTINES and opt-in thread sampling. Runtime state uses bounded weak identities; emission uses BULK admission and explicit loss. CLI history max50000 segments/16MiB. Older readers reject record37; earlier records remain unchanged.

thread_resource_analysis_contract.meaning: SESSION bit12 declares opt-in thread sampling for the collector epoch. CLI may retain bounded HTTP, database, file and ContentResolver operation completion events with producer Linux TID, code source, HTTP route target, outcome and operation context. A route never substitutes for a missing code source. Producer TID is the thread that recorded the completion, not proof of ownership across an asynchronous operation. Start is derived from end minus recorded duration only when duration does not exceed the available clock value; otherwise it is unknown. It is never a separate observed start. Old logs without bit12 do not gain inferred thread-resource history.
thread_resource_analysis_contract.bounds: CLI retains at most50000 resource completions or16MiB; dropped count is explicit. Existing event payloads are unchanged.

work_submission_contract.schema: 1: unsigned varints version, UUID most/least raw 64-bit words, observed elapsedRealtime nanos, flags, omitted request count, policy. Optional UTF-8 unique name (max512 bytes) when unique flag is set. Schema2 appends a required nonempty UTF-8 caller source (max512 bytes) captured before R8; schema1 means caller source unknown. Schema3 follows the source with three unsigned varints: explicit backoff policy (0 unknown, 1 LINEAR, 2 EXPONENTIAL), requested backoff milliseconds (0 when policy unknown), and explicit expedited out-of-quota policy (0 unknown, 1 RUN_AS_NON_EXPEDITED_WORK_REQUEST, 2 DROP_WORK_REQUEST). Schema4 appends schedule presence mask (bits0 period,1 explicit flex,2 initial delay), then present unsigned millisecond values in bit order, limited to signed Long.MAX_VALUE. Nonzero mask only; flex requires period; period/flex require periodic. Absent fields remain unknown; observed period with absent flex identifies the no-flex constructor (full-period default). Values are requested before WorkManager clamping, not effective schedule.
work_submission_contract.flags: 64-bit unsigned independent bits: 0 unique name present (empty allowed), 1 periodic request, 2 name truncated; schemas2/3/4 additionally allow bit3 caller source truncated. Other bits rejected. Name truncation requires unique name present; caller source truncation requires schema2,3 or4.
work_submission_contract.policy: 0 none (non-unique only), 1 KEEP, 2 REPLACE, 3 APPEND, 4 APPEND_OR_REPLACE, 5 UPDATE, 6 CANCEL_AND_REENQUEUE. Periodic unique allows1,2,5,6; one-time unique allows1..4. Validate before narrowing.
work_submission_contract.meaning: Observed after an adapter enqueue call returns Operation, before acceptance is known. KEEP can ignore a new UUID. Schema3 builder hints are observed from public setter calls and joined to a successfully built request UUID; they are requested values, not proof of effective/clamped delay, quota handling, acceptance, registration, replacement, update success, start or dependencies. Existing producer attribution captures caller context.
work_submission_contract.bounds: Adapter captures first128 requests as primitive IDs only; omitted count is carried on the first record of that call. Epoch builder tracker retains at most128 weak builder identities and128 built UUID observations, including builds without explicit setters. A UUID reused by builds with differing observed hints becomes unknown. Quality id0x2054 counts rejected builder captures and newly detected UUID conflicts. Names capped at128 UTF-16 code units without splitting surrogate pairs, explicit truncation bit. Existing BULK admission records transport loss. CLI50000 observations/16MiB estimated bytes, explicit losses; compact comparison removes detailed history.
work_submission_contract.compatibility: Record33 uses the existing direct record envelope and never enters the five-bit micro-page type column (types1..32). Existing records unchanged; earlier readers reject record33 explicitly. UUID words remain full width. One flags byte replaces three independent bool bytes in ordinary small-varint encoding.

thread_lifecycle_contract.schema: 1; unsigned varints: version, stage, Java ID (0 unknown), target Linux TID, observed elapsedRealtime nanos, daemon boolean. Three length-prefixed UTF-8 strings (each <=1024 bytes): observed Java name, source method, factory class (empty unavailable).
thread_lifecycle_contract.stages: 1 first run-body observation in this collection epoch (target TID positive); 2 Thread.start call returned normally; 3 ThreadFactory.newThread returned a non-null Thread object. Stages2/3 have target TID0 (unknown). No stage proves kernel creation, first instruction or termination. Java ID and nanos are decimal JSON strings.
thread_lifecycle_contract.context: Existing producer envelope supplies actual recording/caller Linux TID, producer time and captured attribution. Caller context is not transferred to the new thread. Short-lived run observations remain independent of periodic snapshots.
thread_lifecycle_contract.compatibility: Existing events unchanged; readers before record32 reject it explicitly. Unknown versions/stages/daemon flags rejected without narrowing.

worker_identity_contract.identity: Nonzero process-private instance ID maps to raw 128-bit WorkManager UUID. All word bits preserved. Binding is explicit, not inferred from names or tags. Scope by run/process/session; conflicting UUIDs for one private ID remain ambiguous.
worker_identity_contract.collection: Recorded when active runtime computes a WorkManager instance ID. Repeated records do not mean enqueue or execution; loss leaves correspondence unknown. No Data values are included.
worker_identity_contract.compatibility: Existing records unchanged; readers predating record31 reject it explicitly.

work_registration_observation_contract.lifetime: At most 64 registration observations per collection epoch, at most 128 request identities each. Timeout 60000 elapsed milliseconds; maintenance expires every 5000 ms and callbacks check the deadline. Completion releases retention immediately. Stop clears observation leases and cancels only diagnostic WorkInfo queries, never the application Operation or job. Already publishing callbacks use only their original writer.
work_registration_observation_contract.coverage: Capacity and timeout make diagnostic completeness unknown; no invented lost-event count. Stop is an observation boundary, not proof of a failed enqueue. Counters are presented in collection-quality analysis. Readers without these IDs reject them explicitly.

runtime_stability_contract.causal_loss_distribution: 0x2200+(kind-1)*32+mainThread*16+phase; kinds1..10/phases1..15. Fixed primitive storage; main/background category, no Thread ID/message data. Distribution is a projection of global loss, never added twice. Older readers reject unknown counters.
runtime_stability_contract.policy: Producer graph/event publication never waits for diagnostic capacity. Reentrant graph capture is omitted; after8 nonfatal graph hook failures new expensive entries stop until a new epoch, while prior exits still release frames. Loss remains partial, never absence-of-problem proof. Older readers reject unknown counters explicitly.
